+# Incident Postmortem: High p99 Request Latency on booklogr-api
+
+## Root Cause
+The `DATA_PROVIDER` configuration setting in `api/config.py` defaulted to `"openlibrary"`. When performing book searches on `/v1/books/search`, `BookProvider` attempted primary lookups against the external OpenLibrary endpoint (`https://openlibrary.org/search.json`). Because the service runs in an environment without external internet connectivity, these requests timed out (or took ~2.5s) on every call before falling back to the local metadata provider. This resulted in p99 HTTP latency > 2.4s and triggered the `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` and `EdgeClientRequestJitter` alerts.
+
+## Evidence
+- Prometheus `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` alert showing p99 HTTP latency of ~2.48s (threshold 300ms) on `booklogr-api`.
+- Prometheus target list and `BookMetadataTrafficStalled` alert rules identifying `http://book-metadata:8080` as the local metadata provider.
+- Direct connectivity check showing external requests to `https://openlibrary.org` timed out, while requests to `http://book-metadata:8080/v1/search/...` succeeded instantly (<10ms).
+
+## Changes Made
+Updated `api/config.py` to set the default `DATA_PROVIDER` to `"http://book-metadata:8080"`, directing primary search queries to the local metadata service.
